item.title: US crackdown on tech counterproductive
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
US crackdown on tech counterproductive: China Daily editorial The sanctions and bans imposed by the United States on Chinese technology are seemingly never-ending. In its latest move in the escalating crackdown on China's high-tech sector, the US administration has ordered the removal of all artificial intelligence technology developed by the Chinese company DeepSeek from the IT systems of civilian federal agencies. Announced by the US Department of Homeland Security on Monday, the order bans the use of DeepSeek's AI within civilian government agencies, as well as any technologies developed with the assistance of its models. The department baselessly cited "multiple threat vectors" associated with DeepSeek's models. Several US agencies, including the US Department of Commerce and the Navy, have already banned DeepSeek on government devices. The ban coincides with the US State Department's announcement on Monday of sweeping sanctions under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 against five Chinese entities suspected of "stealing trade secrets" from US companies. Additionally, the US Federal Communications Commission banned the import of all new models of Chinese drones and Chinese-made consumer routers last December. These synchronized moves reflect a broader strategy to gradually "decouple" US technological infrastructure from Chinese technology where the US thinks it is necessary. Under the pretext of safeguarding "national security" and protecting "intellectual property" from foreign "threats", Washington aims to slow down China's AI advances to maintain the US' competitiveness in the global technology arena. In today's world, technological competition is in fact competition between innovation ecosystems. If the US cannot shake China's comprehensive innovation ecosystem, then cracking down on individual technologies and applications will not hold back China's overall technological progress. Chinese AI companies have achieved breakthroughs in model algorithms and technological applications through dedicated research and development within such an innovation ecosystem. Groundless accusations that their success stems from "unfairly acquired technological strengths" are pure slander. For instance, DeepSeek's success can be attributed to its cost efficiency and open-source accessibility. Incorporating DeepSeek into projects costs companies and AI developers only a fraction of what they would pay for a closed-source model like Google's Gemini or Anthropic's Claude. This affordability is why DeepSeek's AI models are widely used by US tech companies and why its free chatbot is among the most downloaded apps in many countries and regions. The US' attempt to maintain its technological dominance through protectionism and administrative intervention is symptomatic of its strategic anxiety. Building technological barriers reflects a zero-sum mindset that is fundamentally at odds with the open, inclusive and mutually beneficial future of global AI development. Healthy high-tech competition drives innovation, while confrontation and "small yard, high fence" policies only hinder collaborative innovation and fragment supply chains without delivering real benefits. Moreover, the recent US actions against DeepSeek contradict the spirit of the consensus reached between the two sides last month, when they agreed on the establishment of the China-US AI Dialogue to exchange views on risks and benefits related to AI, with the next exchange scheduled in November. They also agreed to establish a bilateral communication channel for AI incidents. The consensus was hard-won and should be translated into action and results. No country can address global challenges such as data security and algorithmic risks on its own. China and the US, both major countries in AI, should have the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good, and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the well-being of the people. To that end, the US should abandon its outdated Cold War mentality, respect independent innovations, and leverage the agreed communication channels to manage risks and resolve differences through dialogue.

item.title: APEC economies urged to deepen cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
APEC economies urged to deepen cooperation As a key growth engine, Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation economies should strengthen efforts to uphold multilateralism, deepen open and inclusive cooperation, and unlock new growth momentum to boost the global economy, officials and experts said as the APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting opened in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region on Tuesday. Addressing the opening of the meeting, Lan Fo'an, China's minister of finance, said that as the powerhouse of the global economy, the Asia-Pacific region bears greater responsibilities for global development. "The international situation is volatile and intertwined. Spillovers from conflicts are being felt, and world economic growth faces multiple headwinds," he said, adding that a new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation led by artificial intelligence is gaining traction, with new growth drivers increasing. He put forward three core directions for joint action under such circumstances — strengthening macroeconomic policy dialogue to safeguard regional economic and financial stability, accelerating economic transformation to enhance resilience, and putting development first to promote shared prosperity. "Amid pervasive global uncertainty, APEC members need to ensure sound domestic macroeconomic policies and step up communication and coordination to mitigate negative cross-border spillovers from policy shifts," Lan said. "Economies should also scale up collaborative innovation in AI, the digital economy and the green and low-carbon sectors to foster fresh growth engines." Lan called for more joint efforts to deepen practical financial and fiscal cooperation, foster an open regional economic environment, keep industrial and supply chains stable and unblocked while pushing regional economic integration forward. The APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting is one of the most important ministerial-level meetings on specialized issues under the APEC framework. It is an important platform for Asia-Pacific economies to strengthen communication on macroeconomic policies and financial cooperation. Zhou Mi, a senior researcher at the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation, said that supply chain volatility and the evolving international trade order had placed greater demands on economies' ability to manage risks. "Closer cooperation among APEC members can help cushion the impact of uncertainty, while protecting vulnerable groups is particularly important in a changing environment," Zhou said. Billy Mak Sui-choi, an associate professor at Hong Kong Baptist University's Department of Accountancy, Economics and Finance, said the meeting has brought together representatives from various places to witness firsthand the situation in Hong Kong, which could help strengthen international market confidence in the city. Tang Hei-wai, associate vice-president of The University of Hong Kong, said the meeting serves as a catalyst for joint policy solutions that promote long-term, inclusive growth across the region. Gaby Lin in Hong Kong contributed to this story.

item.title: 'China Haul': Empty suitcases in, packed suitcases out
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
When a British woman suffering from hindered mobility following a stroke was able to discard her wheelchair and walk with the help of a Chinese-made exoskeleton robot at the China Import and Export Fair this week, she could barely hold back her tears. Her son, who was equally overwhelmed by what Chinese technology could achieve, decided to immediately place an order for the device. "I have never seen anything like this in the United Kingdom, or even in Europe," he said. The heartwarming moment was captured on camera, and the footage was widely circulated on social media. Rafael Saavedra, a Venezuelan vlogger attending the fair, described the scene as a glimpse into the future. "Here you can see, touch and test tomorrow's consumer technology — from robots that can run errands to massage chairs," he said. The scene was actually far from unique, as the viral "China Haul" trend has gripped the ongoing China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, which opened in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, on Oct 14 and runs through Nov 4. While influencers have popularized the "China Haul" hashtag on social media, visitors to the fair are buyers searching for China's next-generation products. Across the fair's exhibition halls, foreign visitors were captivated by artificial intelligence-based toys, humanoid robots and other smart devices, with some placing orders on the spot. Their shopping lists tell a broader story. After last year's boom in "China Travel" brought millions of overseas visitors to the country, the latest trend indicates that many are returning home with something more than intangible memories. They are packing their suitcases with Chinese brands — from tech products such as drones and foldable smartphones to lifestyle goods such as sports shoes and AI-powered toys. In other words, China's appeal is moving beyond affordability toward innovation, and that momentum is reflected in official figures. China recorded 23.72 million visa-free entries by foreign nationals from January to August, up 26.8 percent year-on-year, according to the National Immigration Administration. Data from the Ministry of Commerce shows that in the first seven months, overseas visitors spent 263.6 billion yuan ($39.5 billion), an increase of 27.8 percent compared with the same period a year earlier. It underscores a steady recovery in inbound tourism and consumer spending. Speaking on Friday at a news conference in Beijing, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said that China will continue opening its doors wider, allowing more foreign visitors to better understand and appreciate the country through two-way exchanges. The growing enthusiasm for "China Haul" among visitors is also benefiting international retailers. According to Inditex, a global fashion retailer that owns brands including Zara and Massimo Dutti, the share of sales generated by overseas visitors at the Zara flagship store on Shanghai's Nanjing East Road and the Massimo Dutti store on Nanjing West Road has risen more than 10 percent year-on-year. The company attributed the increase in sales to the stores' central locations, the distinctive shopping experiences they offer, their assortment of products, and China's increasingly convenient departure tax refund policy. Taikoo Li, a popular commercial zone in Beijing's Sanlitun, reported a similar trend. The retail complex said the city's continued efforts to improve services for visitors, streamline tax refund procedures and enhance cultural and tourism experiences are attracting more foreigners. "The number of overseas visitors to our complex has seen a clear upward trend," said CT Ma, general manager of Taikoo Li Sanlitun. "International shoppers are interested not only in global luxury brands, but also in Chinese brands that combine local cultural elements with contemporary design. Sportswear, lifestyle products and brands with distinctive Chinese characteristics have become particularly popular," he said. "They are no longer coming only to see China. They are coming to discover what China makes, what China designs and, increasingly, what China creates," Ma said.

item.title: Cultural heritage protection to be bolstered
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
China will step up its cultural heritage protection over the next five years, with a focus on systematic protection, legal safeguards, and bringing heritage closer to people's daily lives, officials said at a news conference in Beijing on Tuesday. The priorities are set out in a five-year plan for cultural heritage protection, issued last month, which aims to build a comprehensive protection framework by 2030 and drive high-quality development in the sector. The plan was also highlighted at the news conference. The plan, which was issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, lists the main tasks for cultural heritage protection in China during the nation's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period. "By 2030, China aims to complete a full survey of its heritage resources, put regulatory systems on a sound footing, improve laws and regulations, expand the talent pool, and make protection oversight strong and effective," said Hu Kaihong, director of the Office of the Central Commission for Cultural Heritage Protection. "A broad framework for cultural heritage protection will have taken shape (by then), fully demonstrating its important role in building a strong socialist culture," Hu added. He said the plan comprises 12 main sections, coordinating protection efforts across cultural relics, intangible cultural heritage, and historical cities, districts and villages, while strengthening the construction and protection of national cultural parks. It covers areas including industrial, agricultural, archival and geographical-name heritage. Hu noted that, based on a clear understanding of the nation's cultural heritage resources, the plan seeks to protect all types of heritage — tangible and intangible, cultural and natural — across all regions and time periods, building a comprehensive national protection system. Historic buildings, districts and villages will be protected as living heritage, with their traditional layouts, streetscapes and cultural settings kept intact. Protection will also become stricter. The legal framework will be strengthened, and work will move forward on enacting a cultural heritage protection law, closing the gap that has left certain heritage types without a clear legal basis, he said. During the nation's 14th Five-Year Plan (2021-25) period, the number of museums in China increased from 5,788 to 7,188. Museums across the country hosted more than 224,000 exhibitions and 2.25 million educational activities, drawing more than 6.2 billion visits. "Visiting a city for an exhibition has become a normal cultural phenomenon, a sign that museum-going has become an important part of people's lives," said Deng Chao, deputy director of the National Cultural Heritage Administration. Under the new plan, "building museums that meet people's expectations" will be the goal during the 15th Five-Year Plan period. A project to improve the more than 6,000 medium-sized and small museums will be launched, in order to enhance their collections and displays and improve the capabilities of their staff members through cooperation with larger museums. "We will channel quality exhibition resources to reach the grassroots level, so that these museums can truly become a core force in community-level cultural services," said Deng. "We hope that traveling for exhibitions will no longer mean only Beijing or provincial capitals. In the 15th Five-Year Plan period, let us look forward to following quality exhibitions to more 'treasure-filled' small cities." As an important category of cultural heritage, intangible cultural heritage resources are increasingly woven into people's daily lives, and more efforts will be made to continue the revival of these resources. Shan Gangxin, head of the intangible cultural heritage department of the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, noted that China is rich in intangible cultural heritage, with more than 100,000 representative items at various levels, 45 of which are inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity — the most for any country. Shan added that China will conduct the second national census of intangible cultural heritage to gain a better understanding of the resources. Furthermore, since the many types of intangible cultural heritage follow different rules of inheritance and development, protection will be tailored to the different types in order to improve transmission and inheritance, he said. For example, traditional performing arts such as opera will be encouraged to revive in new ways, while traditional crafts like embroidery, wood carving and bamboo weaving will transform from "fingertip handicrafts" into "fingertip livelihoods", giving a boost to the upgrading of traditional craft industries, Shan said. More venues for inheriting and experiencing intangible cultural heritage will be built in communities, so that people can learn crafts and watch shows close to home. "In this way, these items return to ordinary alleys and integrate into people's daily lives, and our fine traditional culture can truly take root and grow in people's lives," Shan said.

item.title: Giving shared history a future
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
China and Central Asian countries are building a regional network to safeguard their common Silk Road legacy, report Ma Jingna and Hu Yumeng in Lanzhou. For centuries, Dunhuang, Gansu province, stood at the crossroads of the ancient Silk Road, connecting East and West through trade, travel and the exchange of ideas. That legacy lives on in the grottoes, ancient cities and other heritage sites scattered along the route. Today, it is also driving a new chapter of cross-border cooperation in heritage conservation. The effort took center stage at the 2026 China-Central Asia Seminar on Silk Road Cultural Heritage Conservation, held in Dunhuang in late September. More than 70 experts and scholars from China, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan gathered to discuss a shared challenge: how to exchange conservation expertise across borders while adapting methods to different environments, materials and local needs. For China and Kyrgyzstan, this cooperation is taking shape through a joint laboratory that brings together research, conservation practice and professional training. "The joint laboratory is increasingly becoming an important platform for cooperation between Kyrgyzstan and China," said Aisin Duishanalieva, director of the Republican Inspectorate for the Protection of Historical and Cultural Monuments under the Ministry of Culture, Information and Youth Policy of the Kyrgyz Republic. She said the partnership could expand to include joint heritage monitoring, digital archives, archaeological research, documentation technologies, and professional training. Approved by China's Ministry of Science and Technology in September 2025, the China-Kyrgyzstan Belt and Road Joint Laboratory for Cultural Heritage Conservation builds on nearly a decade of cooperation between the two sides, including joint surveys, research projects and academic exchanges since 2017. The laboratory marks a shift from individual projects and occasional exchanges to a more systematic framework for studying, conserving, and presenting Silk Road heritage.

item.title: Measures set to stabilize finance market
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
Measures set to stabilize finance market Move to enhance liquidity support, facilitate cross-border investment China's top financial regulators pledged on Monday to strengthen financial market stability amid rising global volatility while advancing the sector's opening-up, unveiling a series of measures to enhance liquidity support and facilitate cross-border investment. Speaking at the opening of the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2026 in Beijing, Wu Qing, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, said maintaining capital market stability remains a top priority, warning of growing spillover risks as volatility across global equity, bond and foreign exchange markets becomes increasingly interconnected. To strengthen market resilience, the CSRC will improve long-term performance assessment mechanisms for institutional investors, broaden channels for medium and long-term capital inflows and deepen mutual fund reforms. The regulator approved the registration of the country's first batch of 18 actively managed exchange-traded funds on Monday, a move Wu said will bring additional capital into the market. Listed companies will be encouraged to increase share buybacks and purchases by major shareholders, Wu said, while calling for heightened vigilance against leveraged products traded overseas that are linked to individual A-share stocks. Also at the opening, Pan Gongsheng, governor of the People's Bank of China, the country's central bank, announced plans to establish a liquidity backstop for large-scale redemptions by nonbank financial institutions, as a new macroprudential tool to stabilize the bond market. The facility would be activated under specific circumstances when asset managers face widespread liquidity stress and bond markets enter a negative feedback loop of redemptions and forced selling, while balancing systemic risk prevention against moral hazard. Eligible institutions will include bank wealth management subsidiaries, mutual fund managers and their parent banks or securities firms, Pan said. On financial opening-up, Pan said the PBOC will expand access to its standing lending facility — a monetary policy tool that provides collateralized financing to meet temporary liquidity needs — to cover all domestic deposit-taking financial institutions, including locally incorporated foreign banks. Pan said the central bank will roll out a pilot to allow overseas financial institutions to participate in renminbi trading in China's interbank foreign exchange market and extend access to its RMB repo facility — aimed at helping specific overseas institutions obtain yuan liquidity — to foreign-funded RMB clearing banks. Wu said the CSRC will facilitate investment under the Qualified Foreign Institutional Investor scheme, support domestic and international institutions in collaborating to launch more index products based on Chinese financial assets, and accelerate efforts to include RMB-denominated stock trading counters and real estate investment trusts in the Stock Connect programs. Ding Xiangqun, minister of the National Financial Regulatory Administration, pledged to deepen institutional opening-up, improve the regulatory environment for foreign institutions and encourage their participation in wealth management, pension and healthcare, and green finance. Zhu Hexin, head of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, said the regulator will introduce a package of capital account foreign exchange reforms to facilitate enterprises' cross-border investment and financing, while expanding a pilot program allowing securities firms to conduct foreign exchange settlement and sales. Pan also outlined future monetary policy framework reforms, including studying a shift toward overnight operations as the mainstay of open market operations, making the overnight repo rate the principal policy rate. The PBOC will also promote more diversified loan pricing benchmarks beyond the loan prime rate and further phase out benchmark deposit and lending rates, while promoting connectivity between the interbank bond market and the exchange bond market, Pan added. Also on Monday, the PBOC, together with 10 other departments, rolled out a guideline on enhancing financial support for building global sci-tech innovation hubs in Beijing, Shanghai and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Zhang Linwan contributed to this story.

item.title: Green Long March transforms village in Shaanxi
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
Green Long March transforms village in Shaanxi Share - WeChat
In 1935, the Central Red Army reached what was then Wuqi town in Shaanxi province, bringing its Long March to a victorious end. More than 60 years later, Nangou village in Wuqi county began returning farmland to forest. Villagers went from being reluctant and afraid to give up their farmland to planting trees, shovel by shovel, and tending them day after day. Nowadays, the once-barren hills have turned green, and annual per capita income has risen from 660 yuan ($89.61) to more than 10,000 yuan. The village has opened a campsite and is generating income through ecotourism. From barren hills to green landscapes, and from planting trees to improving livelihoods, Nangou village is creating a "green long march" in the new era.

item.title: Improving demand fuels Q3 growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Improving demand fuels Q3 growth China's stronger-than-expected 4.5 percent economic expansion in the third quarter, underpinned by new growth drivers and improving domestic demand, has boosted confidence that the world's second-largest economy will achieve its full-year growth target, officials and analysts said. The economy's strengthening momentum is expected to extend into the final quarter of the year, they said, as policymakers are directing greater efforts to further bolster domestic demand, with a particular focus on shoring up investment and restoring confidence in the property market. China's GDP growth accelerated to 4.5 percent year-on-year in the third quarter from 4.3 percent in the second, the National Bureau of Statistics said on Monday. Growth in the first three quarters stood at 4.6 percent, within the country's full-year target range of 4.5 to 5 percent. "We expect GDP growth to pick up further in the fourth quarter as growth-stabilizing policies take effect, leaving little doubt that China will achieve its full-year growth target," said Wang Qing, chief macroeconomic analyst at Orient Golden Credit Rating International. He attributed the pickup in third-quarter GDP growth mainly to faster industrial production, which expanded 5.1 percent year-on-year, up 0.4 percentage point from the second quarter. Advanced manufacturing, in particular, accounted for much of that strength. Equipment manufacturing output climbed 10.2 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters, while high-tech manufacturing grew 14.3 percent, the NBS said. Setting out priorities for the sector last month, President Xi Jinping emphasized the need to accelerate the development of a modernized industrial system with advanced manufacturing as the backbone, and to reinforce the foundations of the real economy, in an instruction conveyed at a national conference on advanced manufacturing held in Beijing. The latest figures point to a continued shift toward new growth drivers, said Mao Shengyong, deputy head of the NBS. "Preliminary estimates show that new growth drivers, led by advanced manufacturing, the digital and intelligent economy and modern services, contributed more than 40 percent of economic growth in the first three quarters," Mao said at a news conference in Beijing. Wang Jiaqiang, a senior researcher at the Bank of China Research Institute, said these sectors expanded at around 10 percent, describing their contribution to overall economic growth as "particularly significant". Domestic demand staged a modest rebound in September after softening in July and August. Retail sales — a key gauge of consumption — rose 1.1 percent year-on-year, up from 0.4 percent in August and the fastest pace since March, the NBS said. Meanwhile, fixed-asset investment showed signs of stabilizing, with the year-on-year decline holding at 7.2 percent in the first three quarters, halting a steady slowdown since March. Inflation has edged up alongside stronger domestic demand, with the GDP deflator — a broad measure of economy-wide prices — rising 1.5 percent year-on-year in the third quarter, its second straight quarter of positive growth, said Wang from Orient Golden Credit Rating International. Chen Mengyun, a macroeconomic analyst at Shenyin & Wanguo Futures, said, "The recovery in prices should help lift corporate earnings and strengthen nominal GDP growth." Still, analysts cautioned that the recovery in domestic demand remains tentative, underscoring the need for targeted policy support even as the full-year growth target looks well within reach. Further efforts to stabilize investment will be crucial, said Guo Liyan, deputy director of the Chinese Academy of Macroeconomic Research's Economic Research Institute. She called for closer policy coordination to make the most of the fourth-quarter construction window, with funding from new policy-based financial instruments reaching projects more quickly. Wang from Orient Golden Credit Rating expected stronger, coordinated fiscal and financial support for consumption. He also saw room for broader policy easing to sustain growth into next year. "There is still scope for growth-stabilizing measures, including across-the-board interest rate cuts, to help stabilize the economy," said Wang, who forecast that GDP growth would accelerate to around 4.7 percent in the fourth quarter. Global business leaders are similarly upbeat about China's prospects. Rogier Janssens, president of Merck China, said the company has invested nearly 7 billion yuan ($1.05 billion) in China, its second-largest market, over the past decade. "China's sustained push toward higher value-added manufacturing is modernizing the entire supply chain," he said.

item.title: What stands out in China's sustainable development?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
World Bank director Tatiana Rosito: In sustainable development, what stands out in China's experience? What stands out in China's experience of sustainable development? In a recent interview with China Daily's Global Lens, Tatiana Rosito, World Bank director for China, Mongolia and Korea, said China has "interesting, scalable and replicable" experience in its development, worth sharing with the world. She first affirms China's ecosystem restoration, adding that the Bank and China have worked together on fighting desertification and preventing erosion for more than 20 years. Then environmental solutions: China's experience in controlling air and water pollution is a ready-made example. And the rural-urban link — building sustainable, livable cities and a circular economy — is, she says, exactly the area developing partners most want to work on with China. Under the dual-carbon goals, the energy transition is likewise a good topic for knowledge cooperation. The "knowledge agenda" she describes runs both ways: inward, to help fill China's gaps; outward, using the World Bank's global reach and analytical skills to curate and translate Chinese solutions so other countries can adapt them to local conditions. In the next five years, she expects the World Bank to continue walking alongside China on sustainable development. (Reporter: Li Wei, Video: Pan Yixuan and Cheng Zixin)
